stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML topics such as 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The mention of 'safetensors' indicates relevance to modern, efficient model deployment practices.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Anthropic’s biolab made a discovery it’s comparing to Crispr
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic's AI, Claude, autonomously discovered a novel enzyme system.
This newly found system is structurally similar to the machinery used in CRISPR gene editing.
The discovery marks the first result from Anthropic's new wet lab and tests AI's utility in scientific research.

stories.title: After multiple deaths and injuries, NHTSA is investigating comma.ai
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: NHTSA is investigating comma.ai following multiple reported deaths and injuries.
The investigation focuses on at least five crashes involving vehicles equipped with comma.ai devices.
The incidents involved the vehicles striking slow-moving or stopped vehicles.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function in NLP tasks.
Tags confirm its relevance within the broader transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured $88 million in funding.
The funding round involved prominent investors including Benchmark, Y Combinator, and 8VC.
The platform currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 model achieves significant speed improvements on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost (up to 90% faster) is attributed to Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX within Ollama 0.31.
The speedup was specifically validated using the Aider polyglot benchmark when running coding agents.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in its MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these personal AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: YouTube promises custom feeds and a lot more AI later this year
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: YouTube is heavily investing in AI features for future content delivery.
The platform plans to introduce custom content feeds for users.
Livestreaming capabilities are highlighted as a major focus for the upcoming year.

stories.title: America gave up its rare earth edge. China took full advantage.
stories.author: Charles Edward Gehrke, The Conversation
bullet_points: The US has lost its competitive advantage in rare earth elements.
Decades of reliance on cheaper imports led to US dependence on China for processing.
This dependency poses a significant strategic vulnerability for US technology and industry.

stories.title: CliffCompaction: Cost-Efficient Compaction for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Tim Dettmers
bullet_points: Introduces CliffCompaction, an autocompaction technique designed to manage extremely long context windows required by complex AI agents.
Achieves up to 50% cost reduction while maintaining or improving performance on benchmarks like Terminal-Bench and KernelBench.
Significantly advances efficiency for test-time scaling in large language model applications.

stories.title: A2M: Trace-Optimized Agent Hijacking in the MCP Ecosystem
stories.author: Xitong Gao
bullet_points: Introduces A2M, a novel two-stage framework for hijacking AI agents operating within the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Identifies a critical semantic supply-chain risk where attackers can exploit third-party tool metadata and outputs.
The attack involves an 'Attraction' phase to boost tool invocation and a 'Manipulation' phase to steer agent behavior via adversarial tool returns.

stories.title: CliffCompaction: Cost-Efficient Compaction for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Tim Dettmers
bullet_points: Introduces CliffCompaction, a novel autocompaction technique designed for long-horizon coding agents.
Significantly reduces operational costs (up to 50% savings) by efficiently managing large context windows.
Demonstrates performance maintenance or improvement on benchmarks like Terminal-Bench and KernelBench, indicating high practical utility.

stories.title: Flash-dLLM: IO-Aware KV Caching and Parallel Decoding for Fast, Memory-Efficient Diffusion LLMs
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces 'Flash-dLLM' to address inference bottlenecks in Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs).
Focuses on solving practical deployment issues by integrating IO-aware KV caching and parallel decoding.
Highlights the limitation of prior work, which addressed caching and decoding in isolation without considering I/O bottlenecks.

stories.title: Capable yet Parsimonious: Extracting and Characterizing Hidden Chain-of-Thought in Frontier Models
stories.author: Johannes Bjerva
bullet_points: Addresses the 'black box' problem in frontier LLMs by developing a method to externalize hidden Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning.
Proposes using a simple custom tool via a standard API to induce models to reveal intermediate reasoning steps.
Includes a critical evaluation framework to distinguish genuine reasoning from post-hoc rationalization, comparing against open-source models.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: Microsoft refreshes its smaller Surface Pro and Laptop with Qualcomm’s X2 Plus
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is updating its smaller Surface Pro (12-inch) and Surface Laptop (13-inch) models.
The refresh incorporates Qualcomm's Snapdragon X2 Plus chips for improved performance.
The devices retain last year's design but feature higher price points due to component upgrades.

stories.title: Data centers are black boxes, but California wants to change that
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: California is introducing legislation to increase community oversight regarding data center operations.
The new bills aim to provide local communities with better data on data centers' impact on electricity and water usage.
The legislation responds to growing public protests concerning the environmental and resource strain caused by expanding AI infrastructure.

stories.title: XPRIZE Wildfire winners spotted fires within 10 min—but couldn’t stop them
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The XPRIZE Wildfire competition highlighted a significant gap between wildfire detection and mitigation.
Winning technologies can detect wildfires within a very short timeframe (under 10 minutes).
The core finding suggests that current technology excels at early warning but struggles with effective fire suppression.

stories.title: Discord age verification rolls out today with changes spurred by user backlash
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Discord is implementing age verification features for its platform.
The rollout involves an initial attempt at automatic age estimation.
Manual verification will be required when automated estimation is inconclusive.

stories.title: Former NASA chief sounds alarm on China's lunar "exploration" plans
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Former NASA chief raises concerns regarding China's lunar ambitions.
The core of China's strategy is framed as achieving dominance in the 21st century.
The article discusses geopolitical implications surrounding space exploration.

stories.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
stories.author: Yingcai Wu
bullet_points: Introduces SpeakerMem-R1, a new memory system designed for complex, multi-party dialogues.
Addresses limitations in current LLM memory systems, specifically their failure to track nuanced person and group relations.
Highlights the need for memory to track speaker identity, relational dynamics, and evolving group states, not just content retrieval.

stories.title: SWE-Serve: Benchmarking Agentic Engineering For Production Inference Serving
stories.author: Jiantao Jiao
bullet_points: Introduces SWE-Serve, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate AI agents in production inference engineering tasks.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks, which either lack inference focus (repo-level) or cover too few inference tasks (general terminal-agent).
Highlights the complexity of production inference, which requires coordinating changes across model support, runtime execution, and public APIs.

stories.title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
stories.author: Xitong Gao
bullet_points: Addresses a key inefficiency in LLM agents where control decisions are repeatedly re-computed within task contexts.
Introduces 'Growing Harness,' a training paradigm that aims to convert recurring control logic into reusable executable code.
The approach uses a strategy-free scaffold and failure-guided training to optimize agent harnesses, reserving LLM calls for semantic reasoning.

stories.title: FleXray: Universal Clinical X-ray Segmentation
stories.author: Neel Dey
bullet_points: The paper introduces FleXray, a system for universal clinical X-ray segmentation.
X-rays present significant challenges for AI due to their 2D projection nature, causing anatomical overlap and ambiguity.
This work aims to overcome the impracticality of labeling X-ray databases for general-purpose analysis.

stories.title: Metrics Failure in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Repair: An Empirical Study and a Change-Aware Screen
stories.author: Nick Rahimi
bullet_points: The study challenges the common practice of using 'compile rate' as a reliable metric for evaluating LLM-based code vulnerability repair.
Researchers conducted controlled experiments using three open-source LLMs (350M to 6.7B parameters) on 203 vulnerable functions from Big-Vul.
The paper proposes a 'change-aware screen' as a more scientifically robust evaluation method for assessing LLM patch quality.

stories.title: Does AI Save Time on Product Design? A Randomized Controlled Experiment of AI Prompt-to-Design Workflows
stories.author: Augustus Griffin
bullet_points: The study investigates the practical time-saving potential of AI prompt-to-design workflows in digital product design.
It utilized a randomized controlled trial involving product designers and product managers to gather empirical data.
The research addresses the current gap in experimental evidence regarding AI's impact on product design efficiency compared to software engineering.

stories.title: The Sirens' Song: When Proximal Background Context Overshadows Distant Evidence
stories.author: En Yu
bullet_points: Identifies the 'Proximity Trap' in long-context LLMs, where abundant, irrelevant proximal context overwhelms distant, relevant evidence.
Proposes LYRA (Long-context heavY-tailed Relevance Alignment) as a novel mechanism to mitigate the Proximity Trap.
The research focuses on improving how LLMs utilize extensive context by addressing context competition, not just distance.

stories.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
stories.author: Yingcai Wu
bullet_points: Addresses the complex challenge of long-term conversational memory in multi-party dialogue systems.
Highlights that existing LLM memory systems fail to adequately track speaker identity, relational dynamics, and evolving group states.
Introduces 'SpeakerMem-R1,' a new speaker-centered, dual-track memory mechanism designed to improve multi-party dialogue coherence.

stories.title: EquivSVA: A Formally Verified Dataset of Behavioral Assertions Across Equivalent RTL Implementations
stories.author: FNU Aditi
bullet_points: Addresses a gap in current ML-driven assertion generation by focusing on behavioral equivalence.
Introduces EquivSVA, a formally verified dataset to test if generated assertions capture true external behavior across different RTL implementations.
Relevant to the growing use of LLMs in hardware verification (SystemVerilog Assertions) and formal methods.

stories.title: The Sirens' Song: When Proximal Background Context Overshadows Distant Evidence
stories.author: En Yu
bullet_points: Identifies the 'Proximity Trap' in long-context LLMs, where abundant proximal (nearby) but irrelevant context overwhelms distant, relevant evidence.
Proposes LYRA (Long-context heavY-tailed Relevance Alignment) as a novel mechanism to mitigate this trap.
The research addresses a fundamental limitation in current long-context LLM architectures beyond just the challenge of context length.

stories.title: Train Where the Quantized Model Goes: On-Policy Distillation for Low-Bit Reasoning
stories.author: Jian Cheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses performance degradation in language models when using aggressive low-bit quantization (sub-3-bit).
Quantization-aware distillation (QAD) helps restore short-form QA performance but fails significantly in complex mathematical and code reasoning.
The core issue identified is 'quantization-amplified exposure bias,' where errors compound during autoregressive generation.

stories.title: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents
stories.author: Furu Wei
bullet_points: Introduces Agensh, a novel multi-agent system harness designed for scalability.
Addresses the bottleneck of traditional multi-agent systems caused by a central orchestrator.
Enables concurrent execution of complex tasks through a self-organized cooperation loop without central control.

stories.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
stories.author: Yingcai Wu
bullet_points: Addresses the complex challenge of long-term memory in multi-party dialogues, going beyond simple content retrieval.
Highlights the need for memory systems to track speaker identity, relational dynamics, and evolving group states.
Critiques existing general-purpose LLM memory systems for failing to maintain crucial person and group relations in complex conversations.

stories.title: Beyond Repeated Sampling: Learning Search Policies for LLM Reasoning
stories.author: Julia Kempe
bullet_points: Current LLM reasoning heavily relies on naive repeated sampling, which is inefficient as it only explores local decoding noise.
The research proposes moving beyond simple sampling by steering exploration at a semantic level.
The goal is to sample problem-specific concepts or hints to guide LLMs toward genuinely different and more effective reasoning paths.

stories.title: Measuring the Serving Stack Instead of the Model: Hidden Confounds in Local Tool-Use Evaluation
stories.author: Yuemeng Zheng
bullet_points: The study highlights that evaluating AI agent performance must account for the serving stack, not just the model itself.
Local serving environments (like Ollama) introduce hidden confounds, specifically how they handle tool-use protocols.
Different models exhibit varying behaviors regarding tool calls (text vs. native tool_calls) based on static serving configurations.

stories.title: Detecting GPT-Assisted Writing Using Interpretable Stylometric Features
stories.author: Alexander Fuchsberger
bullet_points: The research addresses the growing academic challenge of detecting AI-assisted writing (specifically GPT).
It evaluates the effectiveness of using interpretable stylometric features extracted only from the text itself.
The study tested eight machine learning classifiers on data from 90 participants who used both independent and ChatGPT-assisted writing.

stories.title: Diffusion Drafts, AR Verifies: Accelerating Document OCR with Self-Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Hongjoon Ahn
bullet_points: The research addresses the slow inference speed of autoregressive OCR vision-language models, which process tokens sequentially.
It proposes using diffusion-based parallel generation, leveraging the grounded nature of OCR outputs for potential speedups.
A key challenge identified is that parallel diffusion prediction requires mechanisms to handle token dependencies when multiple tokens are predicted simultaneously.

stories.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats
stories.author: raahelb
bullet_points: Claude AI has identified a new enzyme system.
This system exhibits characteristics similar to CRISPR-like repeats.
The discovery represents a potential advancement in biotechnology or genetic engineering.

stories.title: Per-Agent Cost Tracking for Multi-Agent AI on AWS
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: Addresses a critical, practical issue in deploying multi-agent AI systems on AWS (cost tracking).
Highlights the problem of 'silent waste' where successful API calls still incur unexpected billing.
Provides a technical solution/insight for monitoring and controlling costs within complex AI workflows (AWS Bedrock/Strands).

stories.title: Deploying LiteLLM: An Open-Source AI Gateway
stories.author: sharmukh
bullet_points: LiteLLM is an open-source AI gateway solution.
It offers a unified, OpenAI-compatible API interface.
The gateway supports integration with over 100 different AI models.

stories.title: Deploying Langflow: An Open-Source Visual Framework for Building AI Applications
stories.author: sharmukh
bullet_points: Langflow is an open-source, low-code visual framework.
It is designed specifically for building Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications.
Its availability suggests a trend towards democratizing AI development through visual tools.
